perspective:
Sara Manuelito’s available information:

- She knows she and Shirley Whiteplume are long-time colleagues and close friends who have worked together at a community health center for several years.
- She knows they are at the funeral of a mutual patient. She observes Shirley’s somber demeanor and suspects Shirley is deeply affected by the loss.
- She hears Shirley say it has been tough, that she keeps thinking something more could have been done, that she feels responsible, and that she wonders if pushing for a different treatment approach might have helped.
- She hears Shirley say she appreciates Sara’s support, but that it is hard to let go and hard to accept.
- She observes Shirley continuing to be reserved and showing minimal emotional expression. She decides to talk with Shirley about holding back feelings.
- She hears Shirley say she is not sure she can open up, that she does not want to seem unprofessional or weak, and later that maybe Sara is right and she will try to be more open.
- She feels her earlier confrontation may have been too harsh, so she apologizes. She hears Shirley say it was a bit much but that she knows Sara meant well and appreciates the apology.
- She hears Shirley say she wants to keep talking because it helps.
- After some time, she observes Shirley’s demeanor improving and feels hopeful. She hears Shirley say she feels better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support.
- She suggests spending more time together outside work. She hears Shirley agree and suggest planning something for the weekend.
- She has access to her own words, intentions, feelings, and actions in each of these interactions.

She does not have access to Shirley’s unspoken private thoughts or any events she did not personally observe or hear about.
